summary: Risk-based review completed. Both controller-declared verification commands succeeded on the exact target digest, but approval is blocked by a frozen-snapshot escape; two additional major compatibility defects affect recovery and engine updates.

findings.title: Tracked symlinks can escape the frozen review tree
findings.description: The target is materialized with `git read-tree --reset -u` without validating or neutralizing symlink referents. The reviewed tree concretely contains `.antigravitycli/f95594b5-b180-4b4d-b9e9-93dd0b5890b8.json` as a symlink to an absolute `.gemini/config/projects/...` path outside the snapshot. Reading that workspace path follows live external content even though the target digest binds only the symlink blob, so the reviewer can inspect data that is neither frozen nor currentness-bound and the referent can change during review without changing the digest. Reject or safely represent out-of-tree links, and classify the known `.antigravitycli` runtime path consistently with the existing volatile-host list.

findings.title: Existing recovery facts become unreadable after the binding expansion
findings.description: RecoveryFact schema 1.0 previously persisted a complete four-field target-binding group (`verification_plan_*` and `machinery_paths*`). This change widens the same all-or-none group to six fields, so every immutable recovery fact written by the immediately preceding runtime has a binding count of four and is now rejected as `incomplete-group:recovery-target-bindings`. `Read-ReviewAuthorityFactFile` validates before reconciliation can recover the process, retire the claim, or remove the snapshot. Accept the former complete shape as a historical variant and degrade currentness as needed, or version and migrate the contract.

findings.title: Runtime updates cannot remove obsolete files, causing a permanent handshake failure
findings.description: `Copy-ManagedDirectory` only creates or overwrites source files; it never removes files left in the managed continuous-review target by an older deployment. The new marker then hashes that stale target exactly, but `Resolve-SpecrewReviewEngineRoot` compares the whole target bundle with the installed bundle. If a runtime file was retired or renamed, update records a marker that includes it, review fails with `review-engine-version-mismatch`, and rerunning the advised update repeats the same state. Prune previously managed files not present in the source (using a managed manifest) before computing the marker.
